title: October Monthly Recap: Organizational Roles, SWIFT Payments, and Events
summary: Along with the platform updates, Slash had an especially busy month of events this October, ranging from a sneaker reseller's reunion to a new billboard campaign.

## October Monthly Recap: What's New at Slash This Month


We had a well-rounded October here at Slash. Along with our usual set of product updates and new features, we hosted and sponsored a variety of events for founders and members of the finance community. If you live in San Francisco or New York City, you may have also seen us on a few billboards. Here’s what we shipped this month:


## SWIFT For Global Accounts


While Slash has long supported SWIFT transfers for U.S. users, it hasn't been possible on our Global Accounts -- until today.¹,³ Slash Global Account users can now send and receive wire transfers to over 180 countries via the SWIFT network.


In addition to SWIFT, the Global Account connects to the US ACH network and local payment networks in the UK, Europe, Mexico, Brazil, and Colombia. It also allows you to send and receive USDC and USDT, two key stablecoins.⁴


In your Slash dashboard, you'll now see some additional fields to fill in when sending a wire across borders:


- SWIFT code
- Account number or IBAN
- Beneficiary name and address
- Recipient bank name and address
- Purpose of payment


To locate the SWIFT code for receiving a wire, navigate to **Add Funds** and select **International wire** . There, you can see the destination details for the account selected, including the beneficiary information, SWIFT code, account number, routing number, and bank details.


Businesses in 130+ supported countries can qualify with their home country’s business registration – no need for a US entity. Connectivity to the SWIFT network is provided by Bridge. Current Global Account users are automatically enrolled, so there's no separate application to start sending wires.


## Organizational Roles and Org Charts


As you develop detailed approval workflows, you’ll probably end up switching to your HR/payroll system to take a quick look at the employee hierarchy on an org chart. We brought those into Slash so you don’t have to make that switch.


We added Org Charts to the Slash dashboard in order to make it easier to map every user’s role on your account and the payment permissions attached to them. Each user on Slash gets a node that connects to the teams that person belongs to. The whiteboard page lays those teams out under the people who manage them, and an employee can trace their team up to the admin or owner in charge of spend approval so they know where to send a request.


This makes it a lot more straightforward to figure out who signs off on what. A new hire on the sales team can open the chart, find their team, and see which manager or admin reviews their actions. Fewer requests land with the wrong approver, and they're less likely to stall while someone forwards them along.


Permissions are also easier to review. If someone changes roles or leaves the company, admins can see every team and payment responsibility that’s connected to the person's node before making any changes.


## October’s Events


This month, there might have been even more going on outside the Slash offices than inside them. Here’s a rundown of the events we helped bring to life in October:


- Calling back to our roots, we brought more than 200 OGs from the sneaker reselling community together for a Sneaker Twitter reunion. Slash was originally created as a banking service for sneaker resellers, and we’re happy that we can get back together with the people that were there from the start.
- We sponsored New York City’s Wrapfest 2026, an event for Jewish founders and investors.
- In tandem with DualEntry, we hosted another Poker Night.
- Alongside Collide Capital and Goodwater, we held a happy hour at Slash HQ for San Francisco Tech Week.
- We covered San Francisco and New York with a series of billboards that stand out from your average, run-of-the-mill tech ads – keep your eyes out for them if you live in the area.
- To cap off the month, we put on a Halloween party for our team at the classic San Francisco Mint.


One of our favorite things to do is sit down with our clients to learn their stories and find out how the Slash platform helped them reach their goals. This month, we had the privilege to hear from[Gravity’s Zach Oldham](https://www.slash.com/blog/rethinking-marketing-and-advertising-in-the-ai-era-gravity) and[Hack the North’s management team](https://x.com/slashapp/status/2111145433284452766) , both representing the forefront of the tech space in 2026.


We have a lot more coming down the pipe, in the form of both product launches and some holiday surprises as we get deeper into the winter. Keep an eye on our website and our socials to see what’s coming next.
